title: What If Raindrops Fell With No Air to Slow Them?
subject: raindrop

scenes.text: What if rain fell with no air to slow it? Every storm would become a barrage.
A real raindrop tops out around 20 miles an hour. Air drag stops it speeding up.
Remove the drag and gravity just keeps adding speed, about 22 miles an hour every second.
From a cloud only one kilometer up, a drop would hit at roughly 310 miles an hour.
That is faster than a Formula One car, from a drop barely heavier than a grain of rice.
So the air above you is not just breathing room. It is the brake that makes rain gentle.
